source.publication: 2025 Maryland Resident Booklet (State and Local Tax Forms and Instructions), Form 502
source.section: Form 502 Lines 1, 13 (Form 502SU code ya), 15-21; Instruction 13 Line 13 code letter ya (PDF page 20); Chart 10A (PDF page 12); Schedule I (PDF page 22)

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = IRA distribution (you) 140,050.00 = 140,050.00. Federal taxable income = 140,050.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000.00 additional for age 65 or older = 122,300.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form 502 Line 1 federal AGI 140,050.00; Lines 2-6 additions 0.00 (no non-Maryland municipal interest); Line 7 total 140,050.00. Form 502SU: code ya (you, age 101): smaller of that person's income 140,050.00 and 100,000.00 = 100,000.00. Line 13 = 100,000.00. Line 14 two-income subtraction: 0.00 (not a joint return). Line 15 total subtractions = Line 13 100,000.00 = 100,000.00. Line 16 Maryland AGI = 140,050.00 - 100,000.00 = 40,050.00. Line 17 standard deduction (Instruction 16, flat by filing status) = 3,350.00. Line 18 net income = 40,050.00 - 3,350.00 = 36,700.00. Line 19 exemptions: Chart 10A at federal AGI 140,050.00 (not over 150,000) gives 800.00 each x 1 (Box A) + 1,000.00 x 1 for age 65 or older (Box B, not reduced by the chart) = 1,800.00. Line 20 taxable net income = 36,700.00 - 1,800.00 = 34,900.00. Line 21 tax, Schedule I as numbers: 2.00% x 1,000.00 = 20.00 + 3.00% x 1,000.00 = 30.00 + 4.00% x 1,000.00 = 40.00 + 4.75% x 31,900.00 = 1,515.25; total 1,605.25. (The tax table row 34,900-34,950, PDF page 36, gives 1,606; expected keeps the formula figure.) Lines 22-26 credits: none modelled or claimed, 0.00; Maryland state tax 1,605.25. Local tax (Lines 28-33) out of scope; 2% capital gain tax (Line 21b) not charged (no gains, AGI under 350,000). Code ya: 'The maximum value of the subtraction modification is equal to $100,000 of income received by an individual', so 40,050 stays taxable. The exemption chart reads federal AGI (140,050, over 125,000 not over 150,000), not Maryland AGI.
